newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish court mulls probing ex-PM on "dirty war".
newsitem.headline: Spanish court mulls probing ex-PM on "dirty war".

text.p: The Spanish Supreme Court considered on Thursday whether to question former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez on allegations he oversaw a "dirty war" against Basque ETA separatists in the 1980s.
Gonzalez, 54, now heads the opposition after his Socialist party lost power in a March election, discredited by the scandal.

Former security chiefs and a disgruntled former Basque region leader of the Socialist party have accused Gonzalez of authorising the campaign of killings, kidnapping and bombings aimed at ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) rebels from 1983 to 1987 in which 27 people died.

In April, a single Supreme Court justice contradicted the opinion of Spain's best-known judge, Baltasar Garzon, and declared in a writ there was no hard evidence to back accusations against Gonzalez and two other top Socialists.
Families of the victims appealed against that ruling and the full court was asked to decide whether Gonzalez should be questioned either as a witness or a suspect.

Gonzalez's first interior minister, Jose Barrionuevo, is trial on charges of creating and funding anti-ETA death squads. Some 800 people have died in ETA's campaign for Basque independence since 1968.
